# v0.9.17 - The Doctor Round: Conflict Copies Found, an Upload Limit Measured, a Real Server Under Test

## What's Changed in v0.9.17

`git-remote-seafile doctor` gains the two server checks a push cannot make for itself: it lists Seafile conflict copies anywhere under the repository path, and with `--upload-limit` it measures the largest single upload the server or its proxy accepts and prints the `seafile.gcmaxpackmib` that fits. `--payload-gc` stops filling the temporary volume and can read a long mark list. `--status` sees two things it used to miss. The real-server tests now run in a throwaway Seafile CE 13.0 container and cover `gc`, the payload store and the proxy-limit probe.

### Added
- **`git-remote-seafile doctor <url>` looks for Seafile conflict copies** anywhere under the repository path and fails, naming each one, while any remain. A copy under `refs/` stops `gc` for good; the `gc` and `--payload-gc` refusals now point at the check, and the RUNBOOK's recovery steps start from it.
- **`git-remote-seafile doctor <url> --upload-limit [--max-mib N]`** measures the largest single upload the server (or a proxy in front of it) accepts. The 1 GiB default pack cap is one deployment's number; a smaller body limit used to turn every large push into a failure after the lock was taken. The probe tries the largest body first (one upload when nothing limits it; 1023 MiB on the measured CE 13.0.28), searches down, reads a proxy that closes the connection mid-body (what nginx does) as a refusal, deletes what it uploaded, and exits 1 when the configured cap exceeds the limit. Against a container whose nginx was set to 48 MiB it found 45 MiB accepted and 48 MiB refused, and suggested a cap of 36.
- **A real-server tier in CI**: a dispatch-only workflow stands up a Seafile CE 13.0 container and runs `tests.test_realserver` against it, including `gc --tail`, a full `gc`, a payload snapshot / restore / verify, `--payload-gc --payload-delete` through its grace period, and the proxy-limit probe.

### Fixed
- **`--payload-gc` / `--payload-delete` could fill the temporary volume mid-fetch.** The run now adds up the remote's packs first and refuses, naming `TMPDIR` (`TEMP` on Windows) and `--allow-low-disk`, when they and the 1 GiB reserve do not fit. The local vault is read where it lies instead of being copied into the scratch repository, so a large vault no longer doubles the space a retention run needs.
- **A `--payload-gc` mark list of about 190,000 entries could not be read**, and the refusal named no way out. The list has its own 64 MiB limit now (about 760,000 entries), and a list over it is refused with the remedy: remove the file and run again, which loses nothing.
- **`--status` could not see a rewrite that kept the mtime but changed the size of a git-stored file.** `mtimes.json` gains an additive `sizes` key that `--status` compares.
- **`--status` printed a newer snapshot's time and "0 changed" after a `--no-push` run** as if all were well. It now has a `pushed` line (`yes`, `NO -- N snapshot(s) were taken after the last push`, or `not recorded`), and `--json` carries `pushed` and `unpushed`.

### Changed
- Each part of the payload hash cache's key now has a test in which it alone stops the cache vouching for an old hash.
- DESIGN §4.3 records a directory listing of 1,100 entries as complete and unpaged, measured on CE 13.0.28.

### Upgrading

Nothing about what is stored changes and no setting is renamed. `doctor <url>` now exits 1 while a conflict copy exists under the repository path, so a script that treats its exit status as health will notice them. A `--payload-gc` run on a volume too small for the remote's packs now stops before fetching instead of failing part-way (`--allow-low-disk` overrides). A vault written before this release has no size record for its git-stored files, so `--status` compares those by mtime alone until the tree next changes, and says so.

The full list is in `CHANGELOG.md`.
